name: Japan
headline: Japan: +1.2% growth in 2025, 3.2% inflation, debt 205% of GDP
sections: Japan is a $4.45 trillion economy (2025), the world's 5th-largest of 215 measured. Real output grew +1.2% in 2025, slower than the world median of +3.5%. Income per person is $55K at purchasing-power parity (2025), against a world median of $21K. Manufacturing accounts for 18.8% of GDP (2024).
Consumer prices rose 3.2% in 2025, broadly within typical target ranges. Unemployment stood at 2.5% (2025), below the world median of 5.1%. Youth unemployment was 3.9% (2025).
Gross government debt is 205% of GDP (2025), a very high level that has fallen from 229% in 2020. The general government balance is −0.7% of GDP (2025).
The current account balance is +4.9% of GDP (2025), a large surplus. Trade equals 45% of GDP (2024), a relatively closed economy. Net FDI inflows were 1.0% of GDP (2025).
IMF projections put government debt at 189% of GDP by 2031, on a declining path from today's level. Life expectancy is 84.0 years (2024). Population: 123.3 million (2025).
note: Built from official World Bank and IMF data; IMF projections are labelled as projections.
